we have proposed an automated approach to relate non-functional requirements (e.g., performance, security, and usability) to architectural concerns (e.g., data, process, and user interface) in software systems, and we have developed a requirements engineering toolset to automate this process.
the ML and NLP techniques are effective in discovering the associations of NFRs and architectural concerns.

developing a method and a toolset to support the automated identification of the architectural concerns from NFRs.
the development of automated requirements engineering techniques to improve software architecture modeling and analysis.

the automation of NFR - architectural concerns associations, which are useful to the requirements engineers and software architects in their day to day practice of requirements engineering and software design.

the approach and toolset presented in this paper is an important step towards the automation of the requirements engineering process.
this approach can be a good candidate as an automated tool to identify and relate NFRs and their associated concerns to architectural aspects in the architectural modeling of software system.

the approach is able to discover new associations and also able to improve its performance over time.

the ML based approach is capable of learning and identifying the NFRs to architectural concerns in the solution domain in an automated way and with high accuracy.

we can automatically identify NFRs and their associations with architectural concerns in a given project.
